# Appendix {.appendix}

## Supplementary Data and Preparation Material

| Source | Provider | Coverage | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Taxi trips | Chicago Data Portal | 2024-01-01 to 2026-04-30 | Trips and pickup demand |
| Spatial boundaries | Chicago Data Portal | Chicago | Community Areas and Census Tracts |
| Weather | Iowa Environmental Mesonet | MDW, ORD and IGQ | Hourly weather context |
| Points of interest | OpenStreetMap via OSMnx | Chicago | Spatial context |

: Data sources used in the analysis. {#tbl-data-sources}

| Variable | Retained range | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Distance | $0 < miles \leq 250$ | Remove zero and implausibly long trips |
| Duration | $59 < seconds \leq 10{,}800$ | Retain trips of about 1 minute to 3 hours |
| Fare | $0 < fare \leq 500$ | Require a positive plausible fare |
| Tips | $0 \leq tips \leq 200$ | Remove negative or extreme values |
| Tolls | $0 \leq tolls \leq 100$ | Remove negative or extreme values |
| Extras | $0 \leq extras \leq 100$ | Remove negative or extreme values |
| Trip total | $0 < total \leq 1{,}000$ | Require a positive plausible total |

: Main plausibility rules applied to taxi trips. {#tbl-cleaning-rules}

| Spatial representation | Units | Geometry | Interpretability |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Community Areas | 77 | Administrative | High |
| Census Tracts | 878 | Administrative | Medium |
| H3 r7 | 163 | Regular grid | Medium |
| H3 r8 | 976 | Regular grid | Low |

## Neural-Network Details

| Role / feature group | Variable(s) | Preprocessing |
|---|---|---|
| Target | `trip_count` | Converted to `float32`; not scaled |
| Spatial unit | `census_tract`, `h3_cell` or `community_area` | TRAIN-only categorical index; unseen units map to index 0 |
| Cyclical time | `month_sin`, `month_cos`, `weekday_sin`, `weekday_cos`, `hour_sin`, `hour_cos` | Cyclically encoded, then standardized |
| Calendar | `is_holiday` | Binary indicator, then standardized |
| Points of interest | `food_drink`, `landmark`, `shop`, `train_station` | Counts per spatial unit, then standardized |
| Weather measurements | `tmpc`, `relh`, `sknt`, `p01m`, `vsby`, `wind_dir_sin`, `wind_dir_cos` | Quality-controlled and imputed before TRAIN-only standardization |
| Weather conditions | `weather_rain`, `weather_snow`, `weather_fog_mist`, `weather_thunder`, `weather_freezing`, `precipitation_trace` | Binary indicators, then standardized |
| Cloud cover | `skyc1_CLR`, `skyc1_FEW`, `skyc1_SCT`, `skyc1_BKN`, `skyc1_OVC`, `skyc1_VV` | One-hot indicators, then standardized |
| Weather-station context | `weather_station_distance_km`, `weather_station_MDW`, `weather_station_ORD`, `weather_station_IGQ` | Distance and one-hot station indicators, then standardized |
| H3 metadata | `h3_resolution` | Included only for H3 datasets, then standardized |

: Target, features and preprocessing for NN training. {#tbl-nn-target-features}

| Component | Input dimension | Output dimension | Activation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Numeric input | $n_{\text{features}}$ | $n_{\text{features}}$ | -- |
| Hidden layer 1 | $n_{\text{features}}$ | 64 | ReLU |
| Hidden layer 2 | 64 | 32 | ReLU |
| Numeric output | 32 | 1 | Linear |
| Spatial bias | Spatial-unit ID | 1 | -- |
| Combination | Numeric score + spatial bias | 1 | Addition |
| Final output | 1 | 1 | Softplus |

: NN baseline architecture. {#tbl-nn-baseline-architecture}

The spatial bias is implemented as a one-dimensional embedding. It represents an
additive spatial intercept rather than a multidimensional representation-learning
embedding. Index zero is reserved for spatial units not observed in the training
split and has no learned effect.

## Neural-network baseline training configuration {#sec-nn-baseline-training}

| Setting | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Datasets | H3 resolution 7, census tracts, and filtered community areas |
| Temporal units | 1h, 4h, and 24h |
| Number of models | 9 |
| Training objective | Mean squared error (MSE) |
| Optimizer | Adam |
| Learning rate | 0.001 |
| Batch size | 1,024 |
| Maximum epochs | 100 |
| Early-stopping patience | 10 epochs |
| Minimum improvement | 0 |
| Checkpoint-selection metric | Validation MAE |
| Output constraint | Softplus activation |
| Numerical preprocessing | StandardScaler fitted exclusively on TRAIN |
| Spatial preprocessing | Categorical mapping fitted exclusively on TRAIN |
| Reproducibility | Dataset-specific seed, starting at 42 |
| Model development split | TRAIN for fitting and VAL for model selection |
| Final evaluation split | TEST remains unused during model development |

: NN baseline training configuration. {#tbl-nn-baseline-training}

            "S×T×W MAE",

## Neural-network baseline diagnostics {#sec-nn-baseline-diagnostics}

```{python}
#| label: setup-nn-baseline-diagnostics
#| include: false

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import polars as pl
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

baseline_checkpoint_path = Path(
    "results/appendix/"
    "baseline_NN_spatial_bias_v1_census_tracts_1h_best_model.pt"
)
baseline_validation_path = Path(
    "results/appendix/"
    "GOLD_1H_DEMAND_CENSUS_TRACTS_VAL.parquet"
)
for required_path in (baseline_checkpoint_path, baseline_validation_path):
    if not required_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Missing baseline diagnostic input: {required_path}")

baseline_checkpoint = torch.load(
    baseline_checkpoint_path,
    map_location="cpu",
    weights_only=False,
)


class AppendixBaselineNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, num_spatial_units):
        super().__init__()
        self.network = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(input_dim, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, 32),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(32, 1),
        )
        self.spatial_bias = nn.Embedding(
            num_embeddings=num_spatial_units + 1,
            embedding_dim=1,
            padding_idx=0,
        )
        self.output_activation = nn.Softplus()

    def forward(self, x, spatial_idx):
        return self.output_activation(
            self.network(x) + self.spatial_bias(spatial_idx)
        )


baseline_model = AppendixBaselineNN(
    **baseline_checkpoint["model_kwargs"]
)
baseline_model.load_state_dict(baseline_checkpoint["model_state_dict"])
baseline_model.eval()

baseline_val_df = pl.read_parquet(
    baseline_validation_path,
    columns=[
        *baseline_checkpoint["feature_cols"],
        baseline_checkpoint["spatial_col"],
        "trip_count",
    ],
)
baseline_features = baseline_val_df.select(
    baseline_checkpoint["feature_cols"]
).to_numpy()
baseline_features = (
    (
        baseline_features
        - np.asarray(baseline_checkpoint["scaler_mean"])
    )
    / np.asarray(baseline_checkpoint["scaler_scale"])
).astype("float32")
baseline_spatial_indices = (
    baseline_val_df
    .select(
        pl.col(baseline_checkpoint["spatial_col"])
        .cast(pl.String)
        .replace_strict(
            baseline_checkpoint["spatial_to_idx"],
            default=0,
        )
        .cast(pl.Int64)
    )
    .to_series()
    .to_numpy()
)
baseline_y_true = baseline_val_df["trip_count"].to_numpy().astype("float32")

baseline_loader = DataLoader(
    TensorDataset(
        torch.tensor(baseline_features),
        torch.tensor(baseline_spatial_indices, dtype=torch.long),
    ),
    batch_size=baseline_checkpoint["batch_size"],
    shuffle=False,
)
baseline_prediction_parts = []
with torch.inference_mode():
    for feature_batch, spatial_batch in baseline_loader:
        baseline_prediction_parts.append(
            baseline_model(feature_batch, spatial_batch)
            .numpy()
            .reshape(-1)
        )
baseline_y_pred = np.concatenate(baseline_prediction_parts)
if baseline_y_pred.size != baseline_y_true.size:
    raise ValueError("Baseline prediction and validation target counts differ")

baseline_abs_error = np.abs(baseline_y_true - baseline_y_pred)
baseline_bucket_labels = np.select(
    [
        baseline_y_true == 0,
        baseline_y_true <= 1,
        baseline_y_true <= 3,
        baseline_y_true <= 5,
        baseline_y_true <= 10,
        baseline_y_true <= 20,
    ],
    ["0", "1", "2-3", "4-5", "6-10", "11-20"],
    default=">20",
)
baseline_bucket_order = ["0", "1", "2-3", "4-5", "6-10", "11-20", ">20"]
baseline_bucket_metrics = (
    pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "demand_bucket": baseline_bucket_labels,
            "y_true": baseline_y_true,
            "abs_error": baseline_abs_error,
        }
    )
    .group_by("demand_bucket")
    .agg(
        pl.col("abs_error").mean().alias("mae"),
        pl.col("y_true").mean().alias("avg_y_true"),
    )
    .with_columns(
        pl.col("demand_bucket")
        .replace(
            {
                label: index
                for index, label in enumerate(baseline_bucket_order)
            }
        )
        .cast(pl.Int64)
        .alias("bucket_order")
    )
    .sort("bucket_order")
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-nn-baseline-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Validation diagnostics for the Census Tracts 1h NN baseline."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

sample_size = min(100_000, baseline_y_true.size)
sample_rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
sample_indices = sample_rng.choice(
    baseline_y_true.size,
    size=sample_size,
    replace=False,
)
sample_y_true = baseline_y_true[sample_indices]
sample_y_pred = baseline_y_pred[sample_indices]
axis_maximum = 175

bucket_names = baseline_bucket_metrics["demand_bucket"].to_list()
bucket_positions = np.arange(len(bucket_names))
bar_width = 0.38

figure, axes = plt.subplots(
    1,
    2,
    figsize=(11.5, 4.6),
    constrained_layout=True,
)

scatter_axis = axes[0]
scatter_axis.scatter(
    sample_y_true,
    sample_y_pred,
    alpha=0.18,
    s=6,
)
scatter_axis.plot(
    [0, axis_maximum],
    [0, axis_maximum],
    color="black",
    linestyle="--",
    label="Perfect prediction",
)
scatter_axis.set(
    title="Actual vs. predicted demand",
    xlabel="Actual demand ($y_{true}$)",
    ylabel="Predicted demand ($y_{pred}$)",
    xlim=(0, axis_maximum),
    ylim=(0, axis_maximum),
)
scatter_axis.grid(alpha=0.25)
scatter_axis.legend()

bucket_axis = axes[1]
bucket_axis.bar(
    bucket_positions - bar_width / 2,
    baseline_bucket_metrics["mae"].to_numpy(),
    width=bar_width,
    label="MAE",
)
bucket_axis.bar(
    bucket_positions + bar_width / 2,
    baseline_bucket_metrics["avg_y_true"].to_numpy(),
    width=bar_width,
    label="Average $y_{true}$",
)
bucket_axis.set(
    title="Performance by demand bucket",
    xlabel="Demand bucket",
    ylabel="Trips",
    xticks=bucket_positions,
    xticklabels=bucket_names,
)
bucket_axis.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
bucket_axis.legend()

plt.show()
```

## Final model test MAE by spatial unit {#sec-final-spatial-unit-test-mae}

```{python}
#| label: fig-final-census-tract-test-mae
#| fig-cap: "Test MAE of final 1h NN models by spatial unit."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import h3
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.cm import ScalarMappable
from matplotlib.colors import PowerNorm
import polars as pl
from shapely.geometry import Polygon

final_model_directory = Path("results/appendix")
processed_data_directory = Path("results/appendix")
prediction_paths = {
    "census_tract": (
        final_model_directory
        / "final_nn_v1_census_tracts_1h_test_predictions.parquet"
    ),
    "h3_cell": (
        final_model_directory
        / "final_nn_v1_hexagon_h3r7_1h_test_predictions.parquet"
    ),
    "community_area": (
        final_model_directory
        / "final_nn_v1_community_areas_1h_test_predictions.parquet"
    ),
}
census_tract_geometry_path = (
    processed_data_directory / "silver_census_tracts.geoparquet"
)
community_area_geometry_path = (
    processed_data_directory / "silver_community_areas.geoparquet"
)
for required_path in (
    *prediction_paths.values(),
    census_tract_geometry_path,
    community_area_geometry_path,
):
    if not required_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Missing spatial MAE map input: {required_path}"
        )

def spatial_test_mae(prediction_path, spatial_column):
    """Aggregate row-level absolute test errors to one MAE per spatial unit."""
    return (
        pl.scan_parquet(prediction_path)
        .group_by(spatial_column)
        .agg(pl.col("abs_error").mean().alias("test_mae"))
        .collect()
        .to_pandas()
    )

census_tract_map = gpd.read_parquet(
    census_tract_geometry_path,
    columns=["CENSUS_T_1", "geometry"],
)
# CENSUS_T_1 contains the complete 11-digit GEOID used in the prediction file.
census_tract_map["census_tract"] = (
    census_tract_map["CENSUS_T_1"].astype("int64")
)
census_tract_map = census_tract_map.merge(
    spatial_test_mae(
        prediction_paths["census_tract"],
        "census_tract",
    ),
    on="census_tract",
    how="left",
    validate="one_to_one",
)

h3_test_mae = spatial_test_mae(
    prediction_paths["h3_cell"],
    "h3_cell",
)
# Convert each H3 cell from the prediction artifact into a polygon. H3 returns
# boundary coordinates as (latitude, longitude), while Shapely expects (x, y).
h3_map = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    h3_test_mae,
    geometry=[
        Polygon(
            [
                (longitude, latitude)
                for latitude, longitude in h3.cell_to_boundary(h3_cell)
            ]
        )
        for h3_cell in h3_test_mae["h3_cell"]
    ],
    crs="EPSG:4326",
)

community_area_map = gpd.read_parquet(
    community_area_geometry_path,
    columns=["AREA_NUMBE", "geometry"],
)
community_area_map["community_area"] = (
    community_area_map["AREA_NUMBE"].astype("int64")
)
community_area_map = community_area_map.merge(
    spatial_test_mae(
        prediction_paths["community_area"],
        "community_area",
    ),
    on="community_area",
    how="left",
    validate="one_to_one",
)

spatial_maps = [
    ("Census tracts", census_tract_map),
    ("H3 resolution 7", h3_map),
    ("Community areas", community_area_map),
]
for spatial_name, spatial_map in spatial_maps:
    if spatial_map["test_mae"].isna().any():
        missing_units = int(spatial_map["test_mae"].isna().sum())
        raise ValueError(
            f"Test MAE is missing for {missing_units} units in {spatial_name}"
        )

# A common normalization makes colors directly comparable across all three
# spatial definitions. The power transformation reveals variation near zero
# without truncating high-error units or changing the values on the color bar.
maximum_test_mae = max(
    float(spatial_map["test_mae"].max())
    for _, spatial_map in spatial_maps
)
color_normalization = PowerNorm(
    gamma=0.35,
    vmin=0,
    vmax=maximum_test_mae,
)

# Use a common map extent so that the three spatial partitions align visually.
minimum_x = min(spatial_map.total_bounds[0] for _, spatial_map in spatial_maps)
minimum_y = min(spatial_map.total_bounds[1] for _, spatial_map in spatial_maps)
maximum_x = max(spatial_map.total_bounds[2] for _, spatial_map in spatial_maps)
maximum_y = max(spatial_map.total_bounds[3] for _, spatial_map in spatial_maps)
x_padding = (maximum_x - minimum_x) * 0.02
y_padding = (maximum_y - minimum_y) * 0.02

figure, axes = plt.subplots(
    1,
    3,
    figsize=(13.5, 5.2),
    constrained_layout=True,
)
for axis, (spatial_name, spatial_map) in zip(axes, spatial_maps):
    spatial_map.plot(
        column="test_mae",
        cmap="YlOrRd",
        norm=color_normalization,
        linewidth=0.18,
        edgecolor="white",
        ax=axis,
    )
    axis.set(
        title=spatial_name,
        xlim=(minimum_x - x_padding, maximum_x + x_padding),
        ylim=(minimum_y - y_padding, maximum_y + y_padding),
    )
    axis.set_axis_off()

color_mapper = ScalarMappable(
    norm=color_normalization,
    cmap="YlOrRd",
)
color_mapper.set_array([])
figure.colorbar(
    color_mapper,
    ax=axes,
    label="Test MAE (trips per hour)",
    fraction=0.025,
    pad=0.02,
    shrink=0.78,
)
plt.show()
```

    paired_values = (
        svm_nn_metrics
        .pivot(index="dataset", columns="model", values=metric)
        .reindex(svm_nn_dataset_order)
    )
    if paired_values[["NN", "SVM"]].isna().any().any():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Metric {metric} is not comparable for every dataset."
        )

    if higher_is_better:
        nn_wins = paired_values["NN"].gt(paired_values["SVM"])
        svm_wins = paired_values["SVM"].gt(paired_values["NN"])
    else:
        nn_wins = paired_values["NN"].lt(paired_values["SVM"])
        svm_wins = paired_values["SVM"].lt(paired_values["NN"])

    winner_rows.append(
        {
            "Metric": metric_label,
            "Preferred value": (
                "Higher" if higher_is_better else "Lower"
            ),
            "NN wins": int(nn_wins.sum()),
            "SVM wins": int(svm_wins.sum()),
        }
    )

winner_counts = pd.DataFrame(winner_rows)
if not (
    winner_counts[["NN wins", "SVM wins"]].sum(axis=1)
    == len(svm_nn_dataset_order)
).all():
    raise ValueError(
        "Winner counts do not cover all comparison datasets; "
        "check for tied values."
    )

header = "| " + " | ".join(winner_counts.columns) + " |"
separator = "|---|:---:|---:|---:|"
rows = [
    "| " + " | ".join(str(value) for value in row) + " |"
    for row in winner_counts.itertuples(index=False, name=None)
]
display(Markdown("\n".join([header, separator, *rows])))

def display_without_index(frame):
    """Render a compact Markdown table without pandas' index column."""
    def format_value(value):
        if pd.isna(value):
            return "--"
        return str(value).replace("|", "\\|")

    header = "| " + " | ".join(frame.columns) + " |"
    separator = "| " + " | ".join("---" for _ in frame.columns) + " |"
    rows = [
        "| " + " | ".join(format_value(value) for value in row) + " |"
        for row in frame.itertuples(index=False, name=None)
    ]
    display(Markdown("\n".join([header, separator, *rows])))


display_without_index(stage_one_results)

## Appendix SVM

### Bug found in cuml
Cuml[@rapids_cuml] appears to encounter challenges when confronted with substantial data sets, resulting in negative R2 values and a progressive decline in performance over time. This seems to happen at with datasets greater than 100_000. Other similar bugs seem to have been found before.

### Steps in developing SVM

These are the changes we made during the developement of the svm in steps and why we decided on them:
- We started with a basic svr on an rbf kernel which is the basic kernel for scikits[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit] implementation of svms.
- Then we added grid search to find good hyperparameter.
- SVM work better on scaled data, therefore we added a StandardScaler[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- Since we were running into runtime issues we changed changed grid search to only include the hyperparameter relevant for each kernel.
- To further counteract these issues we added Nystroem[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- Due to the same reason, we changed GridSearchCV to RandomSearchCV[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- Since we were using a pipeline now we also added the StandardScaler to the Pipeline[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- Since we were still runnig into issues withe the runtime and to get a better performing SVR we added TransformedTargetRegressor[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- For the same reason as before we added cashing(memory) to the pipeline.
- The SVM with the kernel linear was changed to LinearSVM[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- Use cuml[@rapids_cuml, @raschka2020machine] to run model on the GPU instead of the CPU.
- Find a good subset of hyperparameter through testing.
- Changed from RandomSearchCV to HalvingGridSearchCV. Used RandomSearchCV before since HalvingGridSearchCV is still experimental. For our data HalvingGridSearchCV seems to work better[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].
- The scikit-learn LinearSVR, LinearSVC, SVR, and SVC were changed to the equivalent cuml version.[@rapids_cuml, @raschka2020machine] 
- Changed it so y_pred can only be non-negative since trip count can not be negative.

### Pipeline SVR/SVC
- TransformedTargetRegressor (not part of SVC)
- StandardScaler
- Nystroem
- SVR
- TransformedTargetRegressors StandardScaler

### Current Result SVC

![Statistics of SVC](./report_assets/figures/appendix/svc_hexa.png){#fig-heatmap width=80%}

The current result of the SVC does not look good. Due to the focus on the SVR, we were unable to further develope this model[@sklearn_api; @pedregosa2011scikit].

## Appendix: Reinforcement Learning

### Cost Coefficient Calibration
The charging cost at each timestep follows an exponential form: $c_t = \alpha_t \cdot e^{a}$, where $a$ is the discrete action index (0 = off, 1 = low, 2 = medium, 3 = high) and $\alpha_t$ is the time-varying cost coefficient.

We calibrated $\alpha_t$ to match real Chicago home charging rates of \$0.11–\$0.16 per kWh. At medium power (action = 2, corresponding to 14 kW and delivering 3.5 kWh per 15-minute step):

- Cheap end (\$0.11/kWh): $\alpha = 0.11 \times 3.5 \,/\, e^2 \approx 0.052$
- Expensive end (\$0.16/kWh): $\alpha = 0.16 \times 3.5 \,/\, e^2 \approx 0.076$

The coefficient increases linearly across the eight timesteps, yielding:

| Timestep | 2:00 | 2:15 | 2:30 | 2:45 | 3:00 | 3:15 | 3:30 | 3:45 |
|----------|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| $\alpha_t$ | 0.052 | 0.055 | 0.058 | 0.061 | 0.064 | 0.067 | 0.072 | 0.076 |

: Time-varying cost coefficients per timestep. {#tbl-rl-cost-coeffs}

### Hyperparameters

| Parameter | Q-Learning | DQN |
|-----------|-----------|-----|
| Episodes | 20,000 | 20,000 |
| Discount factor ($\gamma$) | 0.99 | 0.99 |
| Learning rate | 0.1 | 0.001 |
| Epsilon (start) | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| Epsilon (min) | 0.01 | 0.01 |
| Epsilon decay | 0.9995 | 0.9995 |
| Hidden layer size | — | 64 |
| Replay buffer size | — | 20,000 |
| Batch size | — | 64 |
| Target network update | — | every 100 episodes |
| Optimizer | — | Adam |
